bull.b: Subscription revenue is a larger, faster-growing recurring stream, reaching 55% of Q2 revenue and growing 34% year over year. This mix can improve revenue visibility and deepen customer reliance on Waystar’s platform, supporting durable expansion over the next several quarters.

TTM gross margin of about 65%, EBIT margin of about 23%, and net margin of about 11% show a shift from prior losses toward profitable operations. Robust operating and free cash flow provide internal funding for product investment and strengthen financial resilience.

Clients generating more than $100,000 of TTM revenue rose 15% year over year to 1,453, while net revenue retention was 108%. These metrics indicate a growing installed base and expansion within existing accounts, supporting recurring growth beyond new-customer wins.

bear.b: Revenue growth slowed to near-flat in 2025 and only mid-single-digit in TTM, while Q2 volume-based revenue rose 3% year over year. Even with normalized growth near 8%, weaker core momentum could limit operating leverage and make guidance delivery more dependent on subscriptions.

Gross debt of $1.5 billion and net leverage of 2.5x leave meaningful financial obligations despite sequential improvement. Debt service and refinancing needs could constrain flexibility if operating performance weakens or AI and software investment require additional cash.

Large platform deals typically require 6–18 months to implement, delaying conversion of bookings into recognized revenue and customer value. Longer deployment cycles can make growth timing less predictable and increase execution demands as Waystar pursues larger multi-solution contracts.
